```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

This tutorial follows `examples/cauquenes/run.R`. Code is not evaluated when
building the documentation because it downloads WorldClim data.

## 1. Study window

```{r}
library(thermify)
library(terra)
win <- study_window(lon = -72.3225, lat = -35.9671, size_km = 20)
win
```

A 20 x 20 km square in UTM zone 18S around the town. It is an experimental
domain, not the commune boundary.

## 2. WorldClim 2.1 (cached)

```{r}
tmin <- worldclim_monthly("tmin", res = 2.5, path = "data")
tmax <- worldclim_monthly("tmax", res = 2.5, path = "data")
tmin <- crop(tmin, win, snap = "out")
tmax <- crop(tmax, win, snap = "out")
check_monthly_climate(tmin, tmax)
```

At 2.5 arc-minutes (about 3.8 x 4.6 km here) the window holds only about 20
cells, too few to represent the Coastal Range and the Cauquenes valley. The
case study switches to the 30 arc-second country tile:

```{r}
tmin <- crop(worldclim_monthly("tmin", 0.5, "data", country = "CHL"), win,
             snap = "out")
tmax <- crop(worldclim_monthly("tmax", 0.5, "data", country = "CHL"), win,
             snap = "out")
```

## 3. Indices for every cell

```{r}
maps <- thermify_rast(
  tmin, tmax, output_dir = "output/rasters", year = 2023,
  temporal = "auto", interpolation = "pchip_mp",
  indices = c("gdd", "ch", "cu", "cp"),
  gdd_methods = c("average", "single_sine", "double_sine"),
  base = c(5, 10), ch_methods = c("sine", "hourly"),
  chill_period = c("05-01", "08-31"), heat_period = c("09-01", "04-30"),
  format = c("GTiff", "netCDF"))
plot(maps$cp_dynamic$season, main = "Chill portions, 1 May - 31 Aug")
```

## 4. Method differences

```{r}
d <- maps$gdd_single_sine_b10$season - maps$gdd_average_b10$season
plot(d, main = "GDD base 10: single sine minus average (degC day)")
```

## Interpretation

* Values are climatological estimates for a reference 365-day calendar
  (2023), not observations of that year.
* Two modelling layers (monthly to daily, daily to hourly) add uncertainty,
  especially to non-linear chill indices.
* The experiment checks computation and quantifies method differences; it
  does not validate any method (see `vignette("validation")`).
